site_gaps.note: Apache license header carries an absolute URL inside a // comment: '//      http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0'. An import-spec-only Go kind table sees no reference here. This exact construct recurs at line 7 of all eight Go files opened for this audit (cobra.go, command.go, shell_completions.go, command_test.go, doc/man_docs.go, doc/man_docs_test.go, doc/yaml_docs.go, doc/cmd_test.go).

Aliased import spec: `flag "github.com/spf13/pflag"`. A detector keyed on a bare quoted string at the start of the import line, rather than on the ImportSpec grammar (optional Name then Path), would drop aliased and dot/blank-prefixed forms. The alias also binds the local identifier used throughout the file (e.g. flag.ParseErrorsAllowlist at line 42), so missing it loses the name binding as well.

Reference-bearing URL inside a Go comment: '// See https://github.com/spf13/cobra/issues/1002'. Same class occurs at command.go:812 and command.go:1627, and repeatedly in command_test.go (lines 1091, 1788, 1808, 1822, 1850, 2269, 2295, 2309, 2424, 2939). Invisible to an import-spec detector.

Runtime-computed output file reference: `filename := filepath.Join(opts.Path, basename+"."+section)`. This is a dynamic file target with no static reference site; a kind table over import specs records nothing for the doc-generation output edges.

Same dynamic-output pattern: basename is derived from cmd.CommandPath() with spaces replaced, suffixed ".yaml" (line 70), then joined with dir at line 71. The generated .yaml path is computed at runtime and unreachable by static reference detection.

`t := template.New("top")` followed by parsing caller-supplied template text; the template body (and any nested template names it invokes) is a runtime value, so no static reference site exists for the template dependency.

Uses package-level identifiers echoCmd (line 47) and rootCmd (line 63) that are defined in a different file of the same package - doc/cmd_test.go:47 declares `var rootCmd = &cobra.Command{...}`. Intra-package cross-file symbol edges require no import spec at all, so an import-only kind table records zero references between files of the same Go package.

Two inline links on one line: '- [Nanobox](https://github.com/nanobox-io/nanobox)/[Nanopack](https://github.com/nanopack)'. A detector that stops at the first match per line would miss the nth=1 site. Line 70 has the same shape (Tanzu Community Edition and Tanzu Framework).
